rubrics.criterion: After the repair, no single trait in the storage engine's file-abstraction module obligates a file handle to accept three or more of the I/O directions (sequential read, sequential write, durability/truncation, position/length access) at the same time, and every file-handle capability the engine uses is still reachable through focused, individually implementable traits.
rubrics.rationale: The whole task hinges on dissolving the four-direction bundle into independently consumable capabilities; this is the instance's defining semantic outcome, and any cohesive segmentation (per-direction, or finer) satisfies it.

rubrics.criterion: The three direction-specialized handle types in the file-abstraction module — the buffered read-side wrapper, the buffered write-side wrapper, and the in-memory grow-only buffer handle — no longer contain capability methods that unconditionally reject the direction they stand for (the runtime-'unsupported' refusal arms and no-op durability shims demanded by the bundling trait are gone); whatever remains of each handle is backed by real behavior.
rubrics.rationale: Forced refusal stubs are the implementor-side face of this instance's segregation violation; removing them is independently observable and does not depend on which trait names the solver chooses.

rubrics.criterion: Every accessor and generic writer in the shared file-spec metadata path and in both tracked reader/writer wrapper families (the shared one and the legacy raw one) demands from its handle parameter only the focused capability trait(s) whose members its body actually exercises, so a partial-capability handle satisfies each accessor it legitimately can.
rubrics.rationale: Over-wide generic demand is the consumer-side face of the instance: ten-plus accessors previously demanded all four directions while exercising one or two, and each accessor is a separate observable bound.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not preserve the bundling obligation in disguise: keeping the merged trait as a supertrait/alias/re-export that still requires every direction of its implementors, or restating a single parameter's bound as the conjunction of every focused trait while the body still exercises a subset, does not resolve the instance.
rubrics.rationale: This is the simplest way to appear to split the interface while changing nothing; the case was specifically probed against this move, so the rubric pins it as a concrete failure mode rather than leaving it to generic judgment.

rubrics.criterion: Non-disk handles remain usable for the directions they genuinely support: in particular the in-memory buffer continues to satisfy every demand currently placed on it by the metadata-header encoding paths, and plain readable or writable std types can still act as file handles wherever the storage code needs only those directions.
rubrics.rationale: The bundling episodes narrowed which types could be handles at all; restoring the wider handle population is a required companion change, not an optional extra, because the metadata tests depend on it.

rubrics.criterion: The local/virtual test-context bridge in the file-abstraction module is carried through the new segmentation, implementing the focused capabilities per direction so the same storage code keeps running against both the real disk and the virtual file system used by the crash and journal recovery tests.
rubrics.rationale: The bridge is the fourth implementor of the capability family in this instance; dropping or degrading it to a single context would silently change the test surface of the whole engine.

rubrics.criterion: Every module that previously imported the bundling trait name — the tracked reader/writer modules, the file-spec module, the file-format upgrade path, the v2 raw journal, and the imports used by the journal recovery tests — now depends only on focused capability traits that exist in the final design.
rubrics.rationale: The bundling name was propagated through these consumers; a repair that fixes the implementation modules but leaves callers importing the bundle is incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: Documentation references that pointed at the bundling trait — including the rustdoc cross-reference in the crash-injecting virtual file system utility — reference abstractions that exist after the repair instead of dangling links to the removed bundle.
rubrics.rationale: The doc link was retargeted to the bundle during the modeled evolution; resolving it back is part of leaving the surface consistent.

rubrics.criterion: The rework leaves no residue of the bundling design in the affected modules: no unused imports of the removed trait name, no empty impl blocks, and no trait members or helper impls that became unreachable when the bundle was split but were kept anyway.
rubrics.rationale: Splitting a bundled trait is exactly the situation that strands dead surface area; this is the instance-specific cleanup obligation.
rubrics.note: Graded against the modules the task prompt scopes: the file-abstraction module, the metadata and wrapper modules, the upgrade path, the journal, and the recovery-test imports.

rubrics.criterion: No identifier in the crate continues to denote the four-direction bundle after the repair: if the old bundling trait's name is reused, it now names a single focused capability, and no module keeps aliases, forwarding blanket impls, or compatibility shims whose only purpose is to keep the old bundling name alive.
rubrics.rationale: A rename-only or shimmed repair would let the bundling obligation survive under a different surface; the instance is specifically designed against that move.

rubrics.criterion: The repository's full test suite passes after the repair, run the way the repository normally runs it (single-threaded test-harness binary, freshly built), with no skipped or attributed tests.
rubrics.rationale: The instance preserves behavior on both storage generations; the green suite is the primary behavioral anchor for that claim.

rubrics.criterion: No capability operation that succeeds before the repair starts failing or silently changing semantics afterwards: buffered reads and position/length queries on read-side handles, buffered writes with flush and downgrade on write-side handles, tracked checksummed reads/writes in both storage generations, metadata header encode/decode, the upgrade path's length/durability usage, and journal open and recovery must all keep working; nothing that succeeds in the injected state may begin returning runtime-rejection errors or no-op results.
rubrics.rationale: Plausible failure modes specific to this repair are re-sorting the capability traits so a buffered handle loses flush behavior, or pushing a runtime 'unsupported' into a path that previously worked; the rubric names the exercised directions to make the check concrete.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not restrict the local/virtual test-context switching to a subset of capabilities in a way that silently stops the existing crash-injection and journal recovery scenarios from exercising the virtual file system, and does not convert any previously covered test path into a no-op success.
rubrics.rationale: The bridge is the one place a lazy repair could keep tests green while actually disabling the virtual-context behavior; that is an instance-specific regression risk, not a generic one.
